Databases

Turn pages into tables, boards, galleries, calendars and timelines.

#Turning Databases on

Databases is opt-in.

  1. Settings → Features → Databases → Show.
  2. A Databases row then appears in the left bar.

#Creating a database

Start from a template (task tracker, reading list, content calendar, roadmap, blank) and choose which pages it covers.

  1. Open Databases and click a template tile.
  2. Rows are real pages. Use the scope selector to cover all pages, one folder or one label.
  3. “New page” adds a row (and a page).

#Columns

Text, number, select, multi-select, date, person, link, checkbox, email, phone, page properties, relations, rollups and formulas.

  1. Press + at the right end of the header to add a column; click a column title for its menu.
  2. Page-property columns (status, owner, date, labels, created, modified, folder) are shared with the page itself.
  3. Relations link two databases; rollups summarise related pages (count, sum, average, earliest…).

#Views, filters, sorting and grouping

Save as many views as you like on one database.

  1. Table, Board, Gallery, List, Calendar and Timeline are the layouts; the + beside the tabs adds a view.
  2. Filter, Sort and Group are on the bar; Properties hides columns.
  3. Drag cards between board lanes, chips between calendar days and bars on the timeline.

#Formulas

A formula column calculates from the other columns of the same row.

  1. Add a column of type Formula and write an expression such as: prop("Estimate") * 100 + if(prop("Done"), 1, 0)
  2. prop("Column") reads a column; use + − × ÷, comparisons, if / ifs, text, list, number and date functions (the column menu lists them all).
  3. A mistake shows “⚠ Error” in the cell with the reason on hover — nothing else breaks.

#Looking in other databases from a formula

A formula can read rows of another database by its name — no relation needed.

  1. lookup("Customers", "Code", prop("Customer"), "Plan") finds the first row of Customers whose Code equals this row’s Customer and gives its Plan.
  2. countIf("Orders", "Customer", prop("Code")), sumIf(…, "Amount") and averageIf(…) count, add up and average over the matching rows; column("Orders", "Amount") gives a whole column as a list for sum(), average() or join().
  3. Names and values ignore capital letters. A database or column that doesn’t exist is named in the error; two databases that look at each other stop with an error instead of looping.

#Charts and dashboards

See how many pages (or how much) are in each group — as bars, columns, a line, a pie or one big number.

  1. Press + beside the view tabs and choose Chart (or change a view’s layout to Chart).
  2. Pick the kind of chart, what to group by (a choice, labels, a person, a date by day / week / month / year…) and whether to count pages or add up, average or find the smallest / largest of a number column.
  3. The chart follows the view’s filters, so “Open bugs by severity” is a filter plus a chart.
  4. For a dashboard, make a page and type /database several times: choose the database and its chart view in each block (the block’s + Chart button adds one). The blocks stay up to date and become tables when you export.

#Forms and templates

Add pages the same way every time: a form with only the columns you want, and templates that fill in the values.

  1. Add a Form view (+ beside the view tabs). It shows a title and the columns that are visible in the view — use Properties to choose them. Press the button to add a page; choose whether the form clears or opens the new page afterwards.
  2. Templates (on the bar) hold starting values, a title like “Bug {date}” and, if you like, the content of a page you copy. “New page” asks which template to start from; a form can use one too.
  3. Templates never change pages that already exist.

#Roadmap view

Themes across quarters, or Now / Next / Later — drag a card to reschedule it.

  1. Add a view (+ beside the view tabs) and choose Roadmap.
  2. Lanes = a Select column such as Theme or Team (or None). Columns = Quarters from a date column, or Stages from a Select column such as Horizon (Now / Next / Later).
  3. Drag a card to another quarter to change its date, to another lane to re-file it. “Earlier” and “Later” show pages outside the window; “No date” holds the rest.

#Scoring and the priority matrix

Rank ideas with RICE, ICE, value ÷ effort or your own weights, and see them on a 2×2 grid.

  1. Press Score on the database bar, pick a method and which columns feed it; Doceo adds a Score column.
  2. Add a Matrix view: pick the number columns across (effort) and up (value). Drag a dot to change its two numbers; the four corners are labelled quick wins, big bets, fill-ins and money pits.
  3. Ideas & feedback (a starter on the Databases page) links feedback to ideas, counts votes and mentions, scores them with RICE and has a button that promotes an idea to an epic.

#Buttons

A button that sets a column, adds a task or opens a page — in every row, or in the middle of a page.

  1. Database: add a column of type Button, then open its menu to choose the text and what it does to that row. Page: type /button, then click ✎ to set it up.
  2. Actions: set a column to a value, set a date to today / tomorrow / next week, add or remove a label, add a task (with a project, due date and priority), add a page to a database, open a page, or show a message. In text, {title} is the row’s title and {Column name} is any of its values.
  3. A button in a page can say which database the page is a row of, so it can set that row’s columns.

#Database automations

Rules that act on a database’s pages while Doceo is open.

  1. Open a database and press Automations → New rule.
  2. Choose what starts it: a page is added, a column changes (optionally to a particular value), or a date column is reached (that day, or some days before / after).
  3. Optionally add a condition (Stage is Open…), then choose the actions — the same ones buttons use.
  4. Rules never run for pages that were already there when Doceo opened, a missed date is caught for a day, and rules that keep setting each other off are paused for a moment.

#Bulk edit, CSV and embedding

Change many rows at once, save a view as CSV, or put a view inside a page.

  1. Tick rows to set one column on all of them or move them to the trash.
  2. The download button in the header saves the visible columns as a CSV file.
  3. In any page type /database, then choose the database and view; Open jumps to it.
